h2: Ultrasonic testing in Phoenix: Arizona's third-party boiler inspections and UT in desert heat
html:
Ultrasonic testing in Phoenix: Arizona's third-party boiler inspections and UT in desert heat

In Phoenix, ultrasonic testing supports two kinds of work: the boiler inspections that Arizona now leaves to authorized third-party agencies, and plant, pipeline and structural scopes where wall thickness or weld quality has to be proven. Atlantis mobilises UT crews from Houston, examines to a qualified procedure with ASNT NDT Level III review, and plans Phoenix work around summer heat.

How Arizona inspects boilers. The Boiler Safety Section of the Arizona Division of Occupational Safety and Health, part of the Industrial Commission of Arizona, stopped performing boiler and water heater inspections itself on July 1, 2017. Certificate and mandatory in-service inspections are now carried out by third-party agencies on the ADOSH authorized list, or by the insurer's state-commissioned inspector where the boiler is insured. Owners remain responsible for getting inspections done and keeping the certificate current, and the state does not send a reminder before a delinquency notice.

The Arizona inspection cycle UT data has to fit:

  • Power boilers above 15 psi: an annual internal certificate inspection plus an external under operating conditions about six months later.
  • High-temperature water boilers above 160 psi or 250°F: an annual certificate inspection.
  • Heating and process boilers at 15 psi or less: every two years.

The section's published scope covers boilers, direct-fired steam-jacketed kettles and lined hot water heaters; it does not list unfired pressure vessels. For vessels in Phoenix plants, intervals usually come from the owner's own programme, an insurer or API 510 where it has been adopted, so the first question on a vessel UT scope is whose interval the data is serving. Atlantis performs the NDE and data review for that programme; it is not an Authorized Inspector and does not sign as inspector of record.

Writing for the third-party inspector. In Arizona the person reading a boiler UT report usually works for an authorized agency or an insurer, not for the owner. Reports are therefore laid out for that reader: the boiler identified as the certificate shows it, drum, header and tube readings at named locations, a comparison with the previous campaign, and any reading below the minimum the inspector set flagged on the front page rather than buried in a table.

Working UT in Phoenix heat. Summer sun can push exposed steel far above air temperature. Sound velocity changes with temperature in steel and changes much more in plastic wedges and delay lines, so a probe calibrated in an air-conditioned truck will mis-measure on hot pipe. Crews calibrate on a block brought to the working temperature, use high-temperature couplant and probes where surfaces are hot, and schedule outdoor thickness surveys for early morning. Couplant also evaporates fast in dry air, which shows up as dropped readings unless the technician watches the signal.

For the wider Phoenix picture, see NDT inspection services in Phoenix and pressure vessel inspection in Phoenix. Weld examination beyond conventional UT is covered by phased array inspection, and the national ultrasonic testing service lists what each survey includes. Local technicians can train through NDT training in Phoenix. To scope UT in the Phoenix area, send the asset list and access window.
